description: Imaris-direct and TIFF-based volume preparation: stream .ims channels to Zarr, build the registration NIfTI from an ims pyramid level with the DL brain mask (no TIFF layer), plus legacy TIFF preprocessing/downsample tools.

rules: Whole-brain production runs must avoid TIFF intermediates. Source data is Imaris .ims (hundreds of GB per file): stream it with ims_to_zarr instead of exporting TIFF folders.

Preprocessing/enhancement (channel_subtraction, median_filter, clahe, tophat, rolling_ball, scattering_removal, surface_brightness_homogenize) is DISABLED by default in production configs: every preprocessing.*.apply=false. Thresholds then operate on raw stored intensities and stay comparable across samples and batches. Only enable a step for a diagnosed, sample-specific artifact.
channel_subtraction is only for samples with a noticeable autofluorescence background; for those the background channel is read from <sample>/chX.zarr (SampleLayout), never from a TIFF folder.

The DL brain mask (pipeline_modules.segmentation.brain_mask_aind, main.py step 1.0) is the ONLY brain-mask source; the Otsu halo mask and edge_signal_removal were removed. Legacy config keys (registration.halo_mask, registration.brain_mask_source, preprocessing.edge_signal_removal) are silently ignored at config load (PreprocessingCfg filters unknown keys; RegistrationCfg uses extra='ignore') so old configs still run.

main.py is TIFF-folder-native but skips steps whose outputs already exist: pre-create ch<signal>.zarr (ims_to_zarr), ch<reg>_downsample/volume.nii.gz (zarr_to_registration_nii) and sample_dir/original_shape.json (full-res z,y,x of the signal grid) to run it with zero TIFF folders.

For the registration channel only a coarse pyramid level is needed: read it with ims_to_zarr --resolution_level N (level N is 2^N x downsampled per axis, e.g. level 2 = 4x per axis; MegaSpim 1.8/1.8/2.0 um native -> ~7.2/7.2/8.0 um) and rescale to 25 um with zarr_to_registration_nii; delete the coarse zarr afterwards. IMPORTANT: a coarse zarr made via plain --resolution_level does NOT carry ims_resolution_level/ims_stride_xyz attrs (only the --reg_channel path writes them), so downstream resolve_input_resolution_xyz silently falls back to native resolution and the 25 um nii comes out ~4x too small (atlas appears magnified). For registration inputs either use --reg_channel, or measure level0/level2 shapes from the ims HDF5 and write the exact attrs yourself.

Deliverables are Zarr/Excel/PNG: keep segmentation.export_mask_tiff=false and registration.save_upsampled_label=false (the label TIFF is written only as a transient intermediate and removed after zarr conversion).
Entry points marked "legacy_tiff": true below are kept for old samples that only exist as TIFF folders; do not use them for new Imaris-based production runs.

library_only_steps.note: deconvolution.py, destripe.py, masked_clahe.py, median_filter.py and rolling_ball_background.py are LIBRARY-ONLY 2D single-image steps of run_preprocessing (pipeline_modules/HE/preprocess.py imports deconvolve_2d/destripe_2d/clahe_array/rolling_ball_background; preprocessor.py imports apply_median_filter/rolling_ball_background). Their standalone argparse CLIs were removed; there is NO independent command line for them — call them through preprocessing.* config blocks or as Python functions.

entrypoints.description: PRIMARY entry point: stream selected channels of an Imaris .ims directly into Zarr (per-channel zarr store, dataset '0'). Select coarse pyramid levels with --resolution_level N (Imaris levels are 2^N per axis) when full resolution is not needed. With --reg_channel N the channel is additionally streamed from coarse level --reg_resolution_level (default 2) into chN_downsampled.zarr with ims_resolution_level/ims_stride_xyz attrs for fast registration downsampling. Resumable; the reference driver _run_YF2025063002_vessel.py step 1 shows usage.
prerequisites: Imaris .ims file must exist and be readable (DataSet/ResolutionLevel N/TimePoint 0/Channel M/Data)
Output .zarr must not exist (or resume an incomplete one)

output.description: Output .zarr path (single channel) or directory root (multi channel)

resolution_level.description: Imaris ResolutionLevel to read; 0 = full resolution

chunk_size.description: z,y,x; matches cfos inference patches; z sets the streaming read slab

reg_channel.description: Also stream this channel from a coarse pyramid level into chN_downsampled.zarr; empty = ask on a TTY, 'none' = skip

compressor.description: default = Blosc zstd + SHUFFLE (clevel 5), fast = lz4, gzip = legacy GZip (pair with gzip_level), none

hdf_cache_mb.description: HDF5 chunk cache size in MB (qc.ims_io.DEFAULT_IMS_HDF_CACHE_MB)

reg_downsampled_zarr.description: chN_downsampled.zarr beside the outputs when reg_channel is set

entrypoints.description: Rescale a (coarse pyramid level) Zarr to the registration spacing and write volume.nii.gz with the production registration NIfTI convention (xyz transpose + UNIT affine — same as preprocessing.downsample; the physical voxel size is recorded in original_shape.json instead of the header; NOT changed here), so ANTs_registration consumes it in place of the TIFF-folder downsample. The DL brain mask is the ONLY mask source: --brain_mask (optional; omit for unmasked registration — no zeroing, no brain_mask.nii.gz, a stale one is removed and ANTs falls back to unmasked behaviour) zeroes everything outside the brain before writing (so registration cannot inflate past the boundary into the scattering halo), is eroded on the registration grid (the former keep-largest-3D-component step was removed as a 0.7-threshold-era workaround; fuse_slab's per-slice size filter already drops strays), and is mirrored into brain_mask.nii.gz beside the volume (N4 + orientation preflight consumers). The old --halo_mask/--no-halo_mask Otsu logic was deleted. An existing volume.nii.gz (and side outputs) is OVERWRITTEN, never refused. Flipping is decided from the sample config: --config reads registration.flip_atlas, the 3-element [ML, AP, DV] booleans already used by ANTs_registration.py; each element flips the volume's numpy axis of the SAME index on this tool's (z, y, x) array — element 0 (ML) flips the stack axis z, element 1 (AP) flips y (identical to the removed --flip_y, which fixed upside-down-mounted xy planes), element 2 (DV) flips x. Evidence: registration/orientation.py::axes_from_flip maps flip[i] to numpy axis i and ANTs_registration._apply_atlas_flip flips the atlas array (index-aligned with the sample volume; the atlas label is later upsampled to the sample original_shape with the same axes, ANTs_registration.py L922); tests/test_registration.py::test_auto_orient_flips_atlas_and_writes_report shows AP=[false,true,false] flipping axis 1. No config / missing key / all-false -> no flip. Writes original_shape.json (full-res z,y,x + spacing + brain_mask stats + flip_atlas) beside the output; copy it to sample_dir/original_shape.json for ANTs label upsampling. Tested in tests/test_zarr_to_registration_nii.py.
prerequisites: Input Zarr with dataset '0' (commonly an ims pyramid level written by convert_ims_to_zarr)
DL brain-mask Zarr on the coarse grid (main.py step 1.0 via pipeline_modules.segmentation.brain_mask_aind); it is required — there is no halo/Otsu fallback anymore

output_nii.description: Output volume.nii.gz path; existing file is overwritten

input_resolution_xyz.description: x,y,z um of the input zarr (native ims resolution x 2^level); use resolve_input_resolution_xyz for ims pyramid levels

brain_mask.description: Coarse-grid DL brain-mask Zarr (e.g. ch0_brain_mask_dl.zarr); the only mask source for the NIfTI zeroing and brain_mask.nii.gz

brain_mask_erode.description: Voxels eroded off the mapped mask boundary (config registration.brain_mask_erode)

config.description: Sample config.json; registration.flip_atlas [ML, AP, DV] decides the volume flip (element i flips numpy axis i of the z,y,x volume). Missing config or all-false = no flip; a malformed 3-element list raises ValueError

output_nii.description: Registration NIfTI (volume.nii.gz, xyz transpose + unit affine)

brain_mask_nii.description: brain_mask.nii.gz beside the volume, same geometry (volume > 0)

original_shape_json.description: original_shape.json beside the NIfTI (original_shape z,y,x, spacing_xyz, brain_mask stats, flip_atlas)

error_cases: FileNotFoundError: input Zarr missing or brain-mask Zarr missing (clear message, no silent fallback)
RuntimeError: Zarr store opens but its data is unreadable by this zarr build (suggests re-export via ims_to_zarr)
ValueError: registration.flip_atlas present but not a 3-element list
Legacy keys registration.halo_mask / registration.brain_mask_source in old configs are silently ignored (the DL mask always runs)

entrypoints.description: Downsample a 3D TIFF stack into a new TIFF stack plus NIfTI volume, using nearest-neighbour interpolation. Legacy TIFF path; prefer zarr_to_registration_nii on an ims pyramid level.

entrypoints.cli: python -m pipeline_modules.preprocessing.surface_brightness_homogenize [--method log_field] --input_dir <sample>/chX --output_zarr <out>.zarr   |   python -m pipeline_modules.preprocessing.surface_brightness_homogenize --method log_field --image <in>.zarr --mask <mask.tif> --voxel_size_zyx 8,7.2,7.2 --field_sigma_um 80 --strength 1.0   |   python -m pipeline_modules.preprocessing.surface_brightness_homogenize --method depth_profile --image <in>.zarr --mask <mask.tif> --voxel_size_zyx 8,7.2,7.2
entrypoints.description: ONE CLI, ONE selector --method, for tissue brightness equalization (merged from the former depth_brightness_equalize module; viewing-oriented, not wired into main.py). USE SCENARIOS — pick --method log_field (default) when the artifact is a slow illumination-like offset measured regionally (uneven staining across the XY field, brighter exterior shell) and the source is a signal TIFF folder or a Zarr volume with a tissue mask (--image/--mask/--voxel_size_zyx, streamed in chunk-aligned blocks); it builds a log-domain regional brightness field on a downsampled or mask grid and scales by (I_ref/field)^strength inside a tissue envelope (sub-modes via --mode: shading = regional log-field normalize, shell = depth gain + local sub-surface suppression). Pick --method depth_profile when the brightness depends on the DISTANCE TO THE TISSUE SURFACE specifically (over-bright surface shell + dark core, scattering halo outside) and the source is a Zarr with a 3D tissue mask: it fits a 1D median-brightness-vs-distance curve on the mask grid and applies the inverse gain, clamped to [min_gain, max_gain], sampled onto the target grid by physical spacing (one downsample fit can be applied to the full-resolution volume).
prerequisites: log_field: either a signal TIFF directory exists and contains TIFF slices (input folder, not an OME-TIFF stack), or --image/--mask share the fit grid (Zarr input)
depth_profile: image and mask cover the same physical field of view; the mask must share the fit image grid; voxel sizes are physical um z,y,x read from the acquisition metadata

input_dir.description: Signal TIFF folder, commonly sample_dir/chX/ (log_field TIFF path; omit when using --image)

output_zarr.description: Default: log_field <input>_surface_homogenized.zarr beside the input; depth_profile <image>_brightness_equalized.zarr (or _depth_gain_fit.json with fit_only)

field_sigma_um.description: log_field Zarr: regional brightness field Gaussian sigma in um

d_max_px.description: shell sub-mode inward surface band, full-res px

d_out_px.description: shell sub-mode outward surface band, full-res px

surface_gain.description: shell sub-mode gain at the tissue surface

tissue_mask.description: log_field: optional manual/SAM tissue mask Zarr or TIFF; skips automatic hysteresis when set

target_scale.description: Both methods: multiply the reference/target brightness

max_gain.description: CLI default is method-dependent; function defaults keep 6.0 / 5.0 respectively

ref_mix.description: Shell I_ref mix in log space between observed surface and interior

output_tiff_dir.description: log_field: also write slices as TIFFs keeping filenames

image.description: Input image Zarr (the grid that is written)

mask.description: 3D tissue mask (TIFF, .npy or Zarr) on the fit grid

voxel_size_zyx.description: Target image voxel size in um (z,y,x)

fit_image.description: log_field Zarr / depth_profile: volume used to fit the field; default is image

fit_voxel_size_zyx.description: log_field Zarr / depth_profile: voxel size of fit_image; default is voxel_size_zyx

bin_um.description: depth_profile: distance bin width in um

edge_gain.description: depth_profile: fixed gain at the innermost mask voxel, blending back to the curve over edge_um (1.0 = off)

edge_um.description: depth_profile: width of the dark edge ramp in microns

apply_chunk_z.description: depth_profile: z-slab size when applying (0 = chunk-aligned auto)

qc_dir.description: depth_profile: write before/after PNG previews here

fit_only.description: depth_profile: fit and write the JSON summary only

overwrite.description: depth_profile: replace an existing output Zarr

output_zarr.description: log_field: OME-Zarr group with dataset 0 (plus preview/pyramid per flags); depth_profile: gain-corrected Zarr on the input grid — both with _run_manifest.json

qc_zarr.description: log_field: sibling *_qc.zarr with a (3+channels, z, y, x) dataset 0 (input, tissue mask, correction/QC planes)

manifest_path.description: _run_manifest.json; depth_profile additionally stamps the gain summary into the output group attr depth_brightness_equalize

error_cases: log_field: PipelineError INPUT_NOT_FOUND (input dir / tissue mask missing), EMPTY_RESULT (no tissue voxels after tightening), ARGUMENT_INVALID (missing --input_dir, mode, chunk_size, or no output target)

depth_profile: PipelineError INPUT_NOT_FOUND / INPUT_FORMAT_INVALID (mask and fit grids differ) / ARGUMENT_INVALID (missing --image/--mask/--voxel_size_zyx, output == input, gain limits out of range, existing output without --overwrite)

entrypoints.description: Add 2x OME-NGFF pyramid levels (1, 2, ...) to an existing 3D Zarr group that already has dataset 0. Needed for napari 3D viewing via napari-ome-zarr.
prerequisites: Input must be a Zarr group containing a 3D array named 0

zarr_path.description: Function parameter name; the CLI flag is --input

method.description: mean for intensity; nearest for integer labels

scale_zyx.description: Full-res voxel size Z,Y,X written into NGFF scale

zarr_path.description: Same store, now with extra resolution arrays and NGFF multiscales metadata

entrypoints.description: ONLY for samples with a NOTICEABLE autofluorescence background: subtract the background channel from every other chN TIFF folder (result = Cx - weight*a*Cbg, optional adaptive global weight fit from tissue non-signal pixels). The background channel is read from <sample_dir>/chX.zarr, resolved via SampleLayout and read block-by-block through pipeline_modules/utils/zarr_io (plane reads hit the store's own chunks); the TIFF-folder background source was removed. Output layout is unchanged: <sample_dir>/chX_subtracted/ TIFFs keeping the original slice filenames. Also available through run_preprocessing when preprocessing.channel_subtraction is configured (legacy TIFF path). Keep apply=false for samples without visible bleed-through so thresholds stay comparable.
prerequisites: Sample root directory exists with chN/ TIFF folders
Background channel Zarr exists at <sample_dir>/<bg-channel>.zarr (e.g. ims_to_zarr or tiff_to_zarr output); the number of signal slices is matched to the Zarr plane count

path.description: Sample root containing the channel folders and the background chX.zarr

bg_channel.description: Background channel label; read from <path>/chX.zarr via SampleLayout

workers.description: Default CPU_COUNT // 2, capped at 61 on Windows

subtracted_tiff_dir.description: Per-channel chX_subtracted/ TIFF output folders under the sample root (unchanged layout)

error_cases: Root path is not a directory -> printed error, no-op
Background chX.zarr missing -> printed error pointing at the Zarr requirement (no TIFF fallback)
Per-slice failures are reported per file; existing chX_subtracted outputs are kept for resume

entrypoints.description: Nearest-neighbour upsample a downsampled mask Zarr back to full-resolution shape guided by a full-resolution signal Zarr.
